properties.Name: Quito, Ecuador
properties.Description: Seat of Ecuador's national government. It passed the 1998 Special Law and prosecuted the crew of the Chinese vessel Fu Yuan Yu Leng 999 in 2017.

properties.Name: Paris, France
properties.Description: Home of UNESCO's World Heritage Centre. It added the marine reserve to the World Heritage Site in 2001 and listed the islands as In Danger from 2007 to 2010.

properties.Name: London, United Kingdom
properties.Description: Home of the Galápagos Conservation Trust, founded in 1995, which raises support abroad for conservation in the islands.

properties.Name: Gland, Switzerland
properties.Description: Headquarters of the IUCN, which took part in UNESCO's 2007 assessment of threats to the islands.

properties.Name: Manta, Ecuador
properties.Description: Ecuador's main tuna port. It links mainland fishing to the islands' marine resources.

properties.Name: Guayaquil, Ecuador
properties.Description: Mainland port city and starting point for much of the migration and tourism travel to the islands in the 1980s to 2000s.

properties.Name: Guangzhou, China
properties.Description: Major southern China market for shark fin. It stands in for international seafood demand that pressures the Galápagos.

properties.Name: Tokyo, Japan
properties.Description: Stands in for Japan's large seafood market and international demand for tuna.

properties.Name: Galápagos Marine Reserve
properties.Description: Created by the 1998 Special Law, it protects waters 40 nautical miles around the islands. It followed a smaller 1986 reserve.

properties.Name: Puerto Ayora, Santa Cruz Island
properties.Description: Fishermen protested fishing limits here from 1994 to 2004. They occupied park facilities, killed giant tortoises, and blockaded the Charles Darwin Research Station.

properties.Name: Seymour Airport, Baltra Island
properties.Description: Main entry point from the mainland. The 1998 Special Law added residency and migration controls to limit population growth and protect the islands.

properties.Name: Isabela Island
properties.Description: Site of Project Isabela (1997 to 2006), which removed goats and other invasive mammals from northern Isabela, Santiago, and Pinta.

properties.Name: Schiavoni Reef, San Cristóbal Island
properties.Description: The tanker Jessica ran aground here in January 2001 and spilled diesel and bunker fuel near Puerto Baquerizo Moreno.

properties.Name: Galápagos World Heritage Site (Marine Reserve)
properties.Description: UNESCO extended the World Heritage Site to include the Galápagos Marine Reserve in 2001.

properties.Name: San Cristóbal Airport, San Cristóbal Island
properties.Description: One of two commercial airports in the islands, with Seymour. Both are regulated by the biosecurity agency ABG, created in 2012.

properties.Name: Galápagos World Heritage Site (In Danger)
properties.Description: UNESCO listed the islands as World Heritage in Danger from 2007 to 2010 over invasive species, migration, and tourism.

properties.Name: Pinzón Island
properties.Description: Site of Project Pinzón (2012 to 2014), which removed invasive black rats from the island. Wild-born tortoise hatchlings followed in 2014, the first in over a century.

properties.Name: Punta Pitt, San Cristóbal Island
properties.Description: The Chinese vessel Fu Yuan Yu Leng 999 was detained about 12 miles north of here in August 2017 carrying 7,639 sharks.

properties.Name: The Galápagos Islands
properties.Description: Volcanic archipelago in the Pacific, about 1,000 km west of mainland Ecuador. It is a province of Ecuador.

properties.Name: Taiwan
properties.Description: Adopted rules against shark finning at sea in 2012, reported as the first Asian government to do so.

properties.Name: Beijing, China
properties.Description: WildAid public service announcements with Yao Ming urged people to give up shark fin soup (2006 campaign).
